tools.name: stamp
tools.description: Recommended agent path. Request a signed, citable statement for a SHA-256 (sit-statement/0.1). Same as the signed-out curl: curl -s -X POST https://soulintime.com/functions/createMoment -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"sha256Hash":"<64 hex>"}'. First one free, no account; one fresh hash per

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Get the signed statement for a hash (sit-statement/0.1). Read-only, no key, creates nothing. On a confirmed receipt the result body carries statement (Ed25519, kid 0a64aa45b8ce17a7; verify offline with https://github.com/SoulinTime/soulintime-client/tree/main/verifier) next to proofFile (.ots). Pend

tools.name: first_at
tools.description: Use verify to cite; first_at only for earliest height. Secondary, read-only: the earliest confirmed public receipt for a hash, optionally at or before a height. Not needed to cite.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "verify" is 7547 chars, far longer than this server's median (1234). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify · Private data: stamp, verify · Public sink: stamp, verify · Destructive: verify.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify · Private data: stamp, verify · Public sink: stamp, verify · Destructive: verify

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "stamp" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
